policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders ‘Shiloh’ and supplies only alternative-rendering notes; neither the verse wording nor those non-textual notes distinguishes the qere שִׁילֹו from the ketiv שילה, so both readings remain compatible and the qere base remains the fallback.
ASV’s ‘his foal’ does not distinguish the qere עִירוֹ from the ketiv עירה; no mapped textual-variant note is given, so both readings remain compatible and the qere base remains the fallback.
ASV’s ‘his vesture’ does not distinguish the qere סוּתוֹ from the ketiv סותה; no mapped textual-variant note is given, so both readings remain compatible and the qere base remains the fallback.
